title: Setting Up Prisma & SQLite
description: Add a database to your Next.js app – install Prisma, define your first model, and run a migration.

slides.title: Why a Real Database? 🗃️
slides.content:
# Beyond In‑Memory Arrays

So far we've stored data in arrays (API routes) or mocked it. In production you need a real database that persists data across restarts, handles concurrency, and offers querying power.

Next.js works great with **Prisma**, a modern ORM for Node.js that supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite.

We'll use SQLite – a lightweight file‑based database perfect for learning and small projects.

slides.title: Install Prisma & Initialise (Terminal)
slides.content: Inside your Next.js project, run these commands.
slides.codeSnippet:
npm install prisma --save-dev
npx prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite

quizData.question: What does `npx prisma init --datasource-provider sqlite` create?

options.text: A `prisma/schema.prisma` file and a `.env` file with DATABASE_URL

quizData.explanation: Prisma init scaffolds the Prisma folder, the schema file, and configures the database connection string.

slides.title: The Prisma Schema 📜
Define the Post Model (prisma/schema.prisma)
slides.content: Add this to the schema and run a migration.

quizData.question: What does `@default(autoincrement())` do on the `id` field?

options.text: Makes the id a random string
Automatically generates increasing integer IDs for new records

quizData.explanation: `autoincrement()` ensures each new row gets a unique sequential integer ID.

slides.title: Running a Migration 🚀
slides.content:
# Create the Database Tables

```bash
npx prisma migrate dev --name init
```

This:
1. Creates the SQLite database file (`dev.db` in `/prisma`).
2. Applies the schema to create the `Post` table.
3. Generates the Prisma Client (type‑safe query builder).

Now you can import `@prisma/client` and start querying!

slides.title: Prisma Client Singleton (lib/prisma.js)
slides.content: Create a single Prisma Client instance to reuse across your app.

quizData.question: What is the purpose of `prisma migrate dev`?

options.text: To apply your Prisma schema changes to the actual database
To deploy the app to Vercel

quizData.explanation: Migrations create and update database tables to match your Prisma schema, keeping them in sync.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content: Always use a singleton pattern for Prisma Client in Next.js to avoid creating multiple instances during hot reload. The code above prevents connection exhaustion.
